problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-7t{y}^{′}+20y=0,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=2,\,t>0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Cauchy-Euler Equations: Characteristic Equations With Complex Roots

examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem Involving a Cauchy-Euler Equation with Complex Roots
examples.problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
2t^2 y'' -2ty' +20 y= 0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y = t(c_1 \cos( 3 \ln{t} ) + c_2\sin( 3 \ln{t}) ),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
2t^2 y'' -2ty' +20 y= 0, \quad y(1)= 0,  \quad y'(1) = -1, \quad t\gt 0.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We find the constants $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1) = 0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0  = c_1.
$$

- To apply the condition $y'(1) = -1,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={c}_{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\operatorname{ln}⁡t)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y'(1) = -1$ and $c_1=0$ into the above to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =3{c}_{2} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & ={c}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(t) = -\dfrac{ t\sin( 3 \ln{t}) )}{3}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x{y}^{′}+25y=0,\,y(1)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-1,\,x>0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+25{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+\lambda +25] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+\lambda +25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+25 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =\pm 5\text{i}.$  

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
y(x)=A{x}^{5\text{i}}+B{x}^{-5\text{i}}.
$$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{5\text{i}} & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{5\text{i}}}={e}^{5\text{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x), \\ {x}^{-5\text{i}} & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{-5\text{i}}}={e}^{-5\text{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =A{x}^{5\text{i}}+B{x}^{-5\text{i}} \\  & =A(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x))+B(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\  & ={c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x),\end{aligned}
$$

where we have set ${c}_{1}=A+B$ and ${c}_{2}=\text{i}(A-B).$  

Now let's find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$

Substituting $y(1)=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
0={c}_{1}.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=-1.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =5{x}^{-1}({c}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-{c}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x))\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=-1$ and ${c}_{1}=0$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =5{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x).
$$
